clue.text: Men turned against officers, absurdly over-decorated

indicators.note: against means placed next to, so the officers sit beside the turned men
turned means the letters for men are flipped round to read the other way

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the military abbreviation for ordinary soldiers
CO is a commanding officer; two of them make COCO

explanation.surface: A mutiny in which the ranks rise against officers who are ridiculously bedecked with braid and medals.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo is the eighteenth-century style of fussy, florid ornament, so the word is used of anything excessively ornate.

clue.text: Pickle bottles tavern put out again

indicators.note: bottles as a verb means holds in, so the pickle contains the tavern

parts.note: a relish is a pickle or chutney
a pub is a tavern

explanation.surface: A pickle maker's bottles are reissued by a pub, as if a tavern were relaunching its own chutney.
explanation.definitionFit: To put out a book is to publish it, so putting it out again is a reissue.

clue.text: About to find out what's for afters?

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for about
to rumble someone is to find them out, informal British

explanation.surface: A child asking what pudding is coming at the end of the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Afters is British slang for dessert; a crumble is a baked fruit pudding topped with a crumbly mix of flour, butter and sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumble is a typical British dessert, an example of what is served for afters.

clue.text: Salmon on the way for party organiser (not sole)

parts.note: the coho is a Pacific salmon
ST is street, a way

explanation.surface: A fishmonger delivering salmon en route to whoever is throwing a party, a catering scene with a fishy pun on sole.
explanation.walkthrough: Sole is a fish too, which sits nicely beside salmon in the surface; here it just means only.
explanation.definitionFit: A cohost shares hosting duties with someone, so they are a party's organiser but not the only one.

clue.text: Herb such as sage, mostly one appearing in meadow

indicators.note: appearing in means the following pieces show up inside the meadow

parts.note: a lea is a meadow, poetic

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word for sage, its last letter dropped

parts.note: sage as an adjective means wise
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A gardener describing a herb like sage growing in a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: Sage looks like the herb of the definition but is the adjective wise; WISE loses its E to give WIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewisia is a genus of small flowering perennial plants from western North America, a herbaceous plant.

clue.text: Primates coming from aristocracy, duke being one

indicators.note: being here means standing as, so the duke's letter is replaced by the letter for one

parts.note: the lords are the aristocracy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Primates as senior bishops drawn from the nobility, with a duke among them.
explanation.walkthrough: D is the abbreviation for duke; swap it in LORDS for I. Primates misleads toward archbishops.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorises are small nocturnal Asian primates; the plural can be the same as the singular.

clue.text: Fairly rich source in need of attention

parts.note: a well is a source of water
a task still to do is one in need of attention

explanation.surface: A rich source of oil or funds that needs looking after.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-to-do describes someone comfortably off, prosperous without being enormously wealthy.

clue.text: One interrupting phone system with personal protest

indicators.note: interrupting means the one breaks into the phone system

parts.note: STD, subscriber trunk dialling, was the British long-distance phone system
I is one
own means personal, as in your own

explanation.surface: Someone cutting into a phone network to stage their own one-person protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A sit-down is a demonstration in which protesters sit in a public place and refuse to move.

clue.text: Extra publicity academic

parts.note: an ad is a piece of publicity
a don is a university academic

explanation.surface: A university lecturer getting a bit of extra publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: An add-on is a supplementary item attached to something, an optional extra.

clue.text: Kids play this at first, once our back is turned

indicators.note: is turned means the letters are churned over into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of once is used

explanation.surface: A grown-up confessing that children were at the game the moment our backs were turned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is turned' rearranges OUR BACK, and 'at first' adds O, the first letter of once.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckaroo! is a children's game of loading a plastic mule until it bucks; the word also means a cowboy.

clue.text: In addition to pennies, I felt something in pocket

indicators.note: in addition to means the second piece is added after the first

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for pence or pennies
ouch is what you say when you feel a sudden pain

explanation.surface: Someone feeling coins and something else in their pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A pouch is a small bag, and a pocket is a pouch sewn into clothing.

clue.text: University near High, but with no affiliation

parts.note: high in spirits means elated

explanation.surface: A university close to a high school but not part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrelated means having no connection, so the thing has no affiliation with anything.

clue.text: Old women graduates containing wild country spirit

indicators.note: containing means the graduates hold the other pieces inside

parts.note: a BA is a graduate; BAS are graduates
the bush is wild uncultivated country
KA is the ancient Egyptian spiritual double, a crossword staple

explanation.surface: Elderly graduates on a trip into the wilds, carrying a bottle of local spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A babushka is Russian for a grandmother, used in English for an old Russian woman.

clue.text: Character no longer granted a service

parts.note: granted means admittedly, though, shortened informally to tho
RN is the Royal Navy, one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A person who is no longer allowed into one of the forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorn is an Old English runic letter, a written character now obsolete in English.

clue.text: Valladolid miss some half-dozen international backs

indicators.note: backs means the extracted letters are read in the opposite direction
some means a few consecutive letters are taken from the words

explanation.surface: A Spanish girl from Valladolid in among half a dozen international rugby backs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes ZENI from half-dozen international, and 'backs' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Inez is a Spanish girl's name, so she is a typical young lady from the Spanish city of Valladolid.

clue.text: Timely preparation for retreat into immorality

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: into means the retreat is put inside the word for immorality

parts.note: vice is immorality
a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: Getting ready in good time before slipping into a life of sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Providence means foresight and prudent provision for the future, so it is preparation made in good time.

clue.text: Volunteers six fur wraps in compound to control bleeding?

indicators.note: wraps means the six and fur go around the volunteers

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral six
mink is a fur
the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Volunteers in a compound wrapped in six fur coats.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitamin K is needed for blood clotting, so it is the compound that helps stop bleeding.

clue.text: To repay with one kiss somehow is this?

definitions.text: To repay with one kiss somehow is this?

indicators.note: somehow means the letters are put together in some new way

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
X is a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Wondering whether making amends with a single kiss counts as atonement.
explanation.definitionFit: Expiatory means serving to atone or make amends, which is what repaying a wrong with a kiss would be.

clue.text: Military command point indeed abandoned

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point
yes means indeed
left means abandoned

explanation.surface: A military command post that has indeed been deserted.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes left is a parade-ground order to turn the head to the left in salute.

clue.text: Superior toy, it hit you, not quite made as required

indicators.note: made as required means the letters are formed into the needed arrangement
not quite means the final letter of the phrase is missing

explanation.surface: A snooty child complaining that a toy hit them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the final U, and 'made as required' rearranges TOYITHITYO.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoity-toity means haughty and snobbish, behaving as though one is superior.

clue.text: Popular woman's appeal to succeed

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable
her is the possessive for a woman
it means sex appeal

explanation.surface: A popular woman's charm helping her get ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To inherit is to succeed to a title or property on someone's death.

clue.text: Each thing critic can have?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... means apiece, each, in informal prices
second meaning: to have ... at something is to criticise it

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are informal British: 'five quid a pop' and 'having a pop at' someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works as a price per item and as a verbal attack, both colloquial uses.

clue.text: What dramatist's done to swap parts that children can be in?

indicators.note: to swap parts means the two halves change places

parts.note: a dramatist writes drama, so the phrase means penned a play, with the writing verb first and the work second

explanation.surface: Asking what a playwright has done to swap roles, with children in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A playpen is a small enclosure in which a toddler can be left to play safely.

clue.text: Ring for help in the kitchen?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a flat ring used with a bolt or tap
second meaning: someone who washes up, or a dishwasher

explanation.walkthrough: Ring for help suggests summoning a servant by a bell; the words split into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a flat ring in plumbing hardware and someone who cleans the dishes.

clue.text: Taking part of the bloke's remains

parts.note: acting as someone means taking their part
he's, short for he is, as the bloke's is short for the bloke is

explanation.surface: Playing the part of a man's mortal remains, as in a funeral drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashes are what is left after cremation, a person's remains.

clue.text: Hate crime: case for officer

parts.note: ABH, actual bodily harm, is a British criminal offence

indicators.note: case for means the outside letters of officer, its casing

explanation.surface: Detesting violence, a crime case handed to a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor is to detest something intensely, a strong synonym for hatred.

clue.text: Post aperitif, initially produce eggs and a rice dish

parts.note: a jamb is an upright post of a door frame

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of aperitif is used

parts.note: hens lay eggs

explanation.surface: After a pre-dinner drink, cooking eggs and a rice dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Jambalaya is a Cajun dish of rice with meat or seafood, from Louisiana.

clue.text: Council promotes area for outing

indicators.note: promotes means the letter moves up, earlier in this down entry

parts.note: a junta is a governing council, especially a military one

explanation.surface: A local council upgrading an area as a destination for day trips.
explanation.definitionFit: A jaunt is a short pleasure trip, an outing.

clue.text: One of fifteen left in race — then one of five

indicators.note: in means the left letter goes inside the word for race

parts.note: to hare is to race along
a quin is one of quintuplets

explanation.surface: Racing results with a horse placed among five and fifteen, read as numbers on a card.
explanation.walkthrough: Harlequins are a London rugby union club; a rugby union side fields fifteen players.
explanation.definitionFit: A Harlequin is a player for the Harlequins rugby club, so one member of a fifteen-man team.

clue.text: Cool, running water, for mud-lover

parts.note: hip means cool, fashionable
the Po is an Italian river

explanation.surface: Cool flowing water appreciated by a creature that likes wallowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippopotamuses wallow in mud and water to keep cool, so the animal is a lover of mud.

clue.text: Last words to sailor recalled? It's not ringing a bell

indicators.note: recalled means the parting words and sailor are called back in reverse

parts.note: ta-ta is a goodbye, last words on parting
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A farewell to a sailor that is remembered, but rings no bell.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat-a-tat is the sound of a knock at the door, made by knuckles rather than a doorbell.

clue.text: Radio broadcast's ending with what Gracie Mansion resident did?

indicators.note: ending means only the final letter of broadcast is taken

parts.note: the possessive simply attaches the ending to broadcast
Gracie Mansion is the home of the Mayor of New York, who ran NY

explanation.surface: A radio show ending with what the mayor did.
explanation.walkthrough: Gracie Mansion is the official residence of the Mayor of New York City.
explanation.definitionFit: Tranny is old British slang for a transistor radio.
